recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Future source changes should be made only if FHIR-I/Vocab approves additional exception patterns or changes the R6 maximum-additional-binding guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-39056 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5. It reported that terminologies.html had an absolute SHALL rule requiring required binding strength for elements with type code despite existing code-typed elements and IG uses with other binding patterns. The final decision kept a SHALL expectation but added the context-free maximum additional binding exception, required FHIR-I approval for other exception patterns, and noted a separate IG Publisher tooling issue.
initial_application: Commit d917880aaa526463777455d7f4e1c55ccb8b7217 initially changed source/terminologies.html and added an ElementDefinition invariant. After the issue was reopened, the invariant approach was abandoned because it produced many validation errors and corner cases. Commit f685fbdd6140f5fc970160305ad3dc4cc72eff83 applied the final prose-only FHIR-I exception wording.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively maps resourceType to terminologies, confirming source/terminologies.html is in current build scope. The current source includes the maximum additional binding exception and the FHIR-I approval rule. Later Applied R6 work for FHIR-46626 added that the context-free maximum additional binding combination is strongly discouraged as of R6, refining but not reversing FHIR-39056.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/terminologies.html already conveys that required binding strength is expected for type code unless the context-free maximum additional binding exception applies, and that other exceptions require FHIR-I approval. Adding the exact phrase 'In most cases' would be redundant and could obscure the later R6 qualifier.

related_jiras.note: Applied R6 change added the 'strongly discouraged as of R6' qualifier to the same maximum-additional-binding exception without reversing FHIR-39056.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive with Modification issue requiring the required-code-binding rule to allow a context-free maximum additional binding exception and FHIR-I-approved exception patterns.
evidence_items.learned: This establishes the final rule that the current terminology source must convey.

evidence_items.summary: The type-page configuration maps resourceType to terminologies.
evidence_items.learned: The terminologies page source is part of the current build scope.

evidence_items.summary: The current prose states the required binding expectation for type code, the context-free maximum additional binding exception, the R6 discouragement note, and the FHIR-I approval rule for exceptions.
evidence_items.learned: The current source already implements the resolved semantic rule, with later R6 context preserved.

evidence_items.summary: The first FHIR-39056 commit added narrative plus an invariant; the later FHIR-39056 commit removed the invariant reference and added FHIR-I exception prose.
evidence_items.learned: Initial application was corrected before publication, so a missing invariant is not a current defect.

evidence_items.summary: Grahame Grieve said the invariant caused hundreds of validation errors and corner cases made it too hard.

evidence_items.summary: FHIR-I minutes record reopening FHIR-39056, sticking with SHALL while adding 'in most cases', and approving Persuasive with Modification 13-0-1.
evidence_items.learned: The intended outcome is a SHALL expectation qualified by documented exceptions, not a hard invariant.

evidence_items.summary: Applied R6 work changed maximum-additional-binding terminology and added that this exception combination is strongly discouraged as of R6.
evidence_items.learned: The current qualifier is later governing context and should be preserved when auditing FHIR-39056.
